summary: Mobile tether (iPhone) establishing IPv6 SLAAC route leak that overrides VPN routes and prevents access to internal services
description:
Issue summary: When an internal engineer tethered their iPhone to test at-home connectivity, macOS accepted an IPv6 SLAAC prefix from the tethered interface and installed a higher-priority route that superseded corporate VPN routes. Impact: Unable to reach internal-only services (service.example.redwood) while VPN shows as connected. This appears tied to RA (Router Advertisement) received over the mobile tether (iPhone 15 Pro) and the default route selection behavior on macOS + our VPN client.

Observed: Internal hostnames time out or resolve to private v6 addresses that are unreachable via the VPN path. VPN tunnel remains established (no visible drop), but traffic leaks to the tether interface and is dropped by carrier or local stack.

Expected: When the Redwood VPN is active, internal prefixes and routes pushed by the VPN should take precedence over any ephemeral IPv6 routes from tethered clients. Mobile tethering should not silently override VPN-scoped routes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) macOS 13/14 laptop with Redwood VPN client connected to corp VPN (tunnel up, internal routes present).
2) Enable iPhone personal hotspot (mobile tether) and connect laptop via Wi‑Fi hotspot.
3) Observe 'ifconfig' and 'netstat -rn' or 'ip -6 route' showing new SLAAC prefix on wlan or en0.
4) Attempt to curl or SSH internal hostname (service.example.redwood) — connections fail/timeout despite VPN up.
5) Remove tethered interface or disable IPv6 on tether interface; connectivity to internal services is restored.
observed_behavior: macOS kernel installs a ::/64 route learned by SLAAC from the tether that has a more specific/identical metric and higher precedence than the VPN-provisioned route.
Redwood VPN process reports tunnel up, and push routes are present in VPN client logs, but the system chooses the tethered interface for some destination v6 prefixes.
DNS for internal hostnames resolves to v6 addresses (AAAA) which are attempted over the tethered path and get RST or time out.
expected_behavior: VPN-provisioned internal prefixes (v4 and v6) should be preferred and route traffic for internal hosts through the tunnel, even when a tethered interface introduces RA/SLAAC addresses.
At minimum there should be a clear fail-safe: when VPN is active, accept RA-derived routes only if they do not overlap internal/prefixes or are lower priority.
logs: VPN client log excerpt (2026-03-10T09:12:33Z): [info] tunnel established; pushed routes: 10.0.0.0/8 via tun0, fd00:dead:beef::/48 via tun0
syslog excerpt (kernel): detected RA on en0 from fe80::1; autoconf assigned 2601:abcd:1234:1::abcd/64
netstat -rn before tether: ::/0 via fe80::a dev tun0, fd00:dead:beef::/48 dev tun0
netstat -rn after tether: 2601:abcd:1234::/64 dev en0  (precedence 0x8000)  -- masks/metric cause kernel to select en0 for AAAA destinations
tcpdump -i en0 icmp6: 02:14:22.123456 IP6 fe80::1 > ff02::1:ff00:1: ICMP6, router advertisement, length 64
investigation_notes: Confirmed issue reproducible on two macOS laptops (13.6 and 14.1) and one Linux laptop where NetworkManager behaved differently (Linux defaults to preferring VPN routes).

Hypothesis: macOS prefers on-link routes learned by RA over tunnel routes when both exist due to route selection and scope rules. VPN client currently relies on pushing a /48 internal prefix that overlaps (or is a superset of) SLAAC /64s, but the kernel chooses the on-link /64 for specific destinations.
Checked iPhone hotspot behavior: iOS advertises a /64 via RA when offering IPv6 tethering; carrier does not NAT v6, so actual path leaves the phone and is not routable to our internal network.
temporary_workarounds: Manual: On affected macOS clients run: sudo route -nv add -inet6 fd00:dead:beef::/48 -interface tun0 (or use 'networksetup -setv6off <device>' to disable IPv6 on the Wi‑Fi interface).
Advisory: Avoid connecting to mobile hotspots while VPN is required for internal service access until fix is in place.
On Linux: ip -6 rule add pref 1000 from all lookup vpn-table to prefer VPN when present.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Customer reproducible. I tethered an iPhone and saw SLAAC prefix installed; internal services unreachable while VPN showed connected. Captured tcpdump and route tables attached.

Liam Chen (2026-03-11): I reproduced on my MacBook. VPN client shows fd00:dead:beef::/48 in pushed routes but kernel prefers on-link /64. Opening thread with SRE networking to confirm precedence semantics.

SRE-Networking (2026-03-11): Noted macOS route precedence: on-link routes win for exact matches. Recommend two remediation paths: 1) have VPN client install more specific /64 host route(s) for internal v6 endpoints, or 2) manipulate route metrics/precedence from the client (add RTF_CONNECTED flag adjustments) — need product input on acceptable client behavior.
Security (2026-03-12): Concern: disabling IPv6 on Wi‑Fi automatically may have unintended side effects. Prefer client-side safe route adjustments.
Liam Chen (2026-03-13): Created prototype patch to add explicit host/64 routes for critical internal AAAA records when tunnel is established. Patch: PR #4532. Rolling to staging for QA.
next_steps: QA the prototype patch in staging with IPv6 mobile tether test cases (Liam + SRE).
If patch validates, schedule a non-disruptive client release with explicit host routes for internal AAAA entries and update runbook.
Long-term: design VPN client option to prefer tunnel-provisioned prefixes and document behavior for mobile tether scenarios.
